How it works

Two loops.
One conversation.

One loop handles continuous perception and speech. The other executes delegated tasks and prepares replies. Both stay connected to the same conversation.

9B · Audio + video

Realtime-Venus-Omni

Follow visual events, respond proactively, and recall relevant context from long videos.

9B · Audio

Realtime-Venus-Audio

Understand sound and speech, generate spoken responses, and distinguish interruptions from backchannels.

Background execution

Realtime-Venus-Harness

Capture the request’s context, run external capabilities, and prepare a reply for the frontend to speak.

Inside the systemTask delivery, training, and long-video memoryExpandCollapse
1

Capture the right context

Capture the evidence available when a request begins, and keep it bound to its originating conversation.

2

Keep interaction running

Route tasks to multimodal, general, or registered skill backends while perception and dialogue continue.

3

Bring results back in time

The harness prepares the reply; the frontend chooses when to speak it. Delivery tracking confirms that the generated speech has been played.

Learn timing and delegation together

A shared post-training recipe combines offline understanding, proactive full-duplex trajectories, and delegation workflows. Aligned conversation data includes pauses, backchannels, interruptions, and background tasks, connecting what to say with when to speak.

Long-video memory

Keep useful context within reach

Realtime-Venus-Omni adds a training-free memory module for extended audio–visual sessions. It stores selected historical frames, retrieves evidence using relevance and novelty, and combines recalled context with recent observations.

The memory module is separate from the fine-tuned dialogue policy and requires no additional parameter updates.

What delegation measures

The in-house Delegate Benchmark reports routing accuracy of 75.93% for Omni and 68.89% for Audio. A correct decision to use a capability is distinct from successful task completion; audio-only and audio–visual settings also have different inputs and difficulty levels. These results should be interpreted within their respective evaluation protocols.
